blurb: Tall Afghan sighthound with a long silky coat and a ring-curled tail
description: The Afghan Hound is a tall sighthound from the mountains of Afghanistan, known for its long, fine, silky coat and an aloof yet playful temperament.
answer: The Afghan Hound is a sighthound from the cold mountains of Afghanistan, bred for speed and hunting game. It typically stands about 63 to 74 cm tall and weighs around 23 to 27 kg. It is often described as aloof and dignified, with a clownish side when playing.

body: The Afghan Hound has been identified as a basal breed that predates most modern breeds and is most closely related to the Saluki. Sighthounds from the region reached England in the 1800s with returning army officers. Two strains shaped the modern breed: the less heavily coated Bell-Murray dogs brought to Scotland in 1920 and the heavily coated Ghazni dogs shipped from Kabul by Mary Amps in 1925. A new standard written in 1948 is still in use. The breed is no longer used for hunting but appears in lure coursing.

This is a tall dog with high hipbones and a small ring at the end of the tail. The long, fine-textured coat may be any color, and many dogs have a black facial mask. A long topknot and a shorter-haired saddle on the back are distinctive features. The coat is said to have developed as protection from the harsh mountain climate.

The American Kennel Club describes the breed as an aloof and dignified aristocrat with an endearing streak of silliness and profound loyalty. Like other sighthounds it has a high prey drive and may chase or kill small animals. Trainers surveyed by Stanley Coren ranked it among the least obedient breeds.

The long coat requires considerable care and regular grooming. Sources give little detail on exercise needs, though as a sighthound bred for speed it is generally expected to need room to run in a safe, enclosed space.

Conditions reported in the breed include allergies, cancer, hip dysplasia, chylothorax, laryngeal paralysis, dilated cardiomyopathy, hypothyroidism, cataract and progressive retinal atrophy. Like other sighthounds it is noted as sensitive to anesthesia. One UK study found a life expectancy of 11.1 years.

faq.q: How big does an Afghan Hound get?
faq.a: Afghan Hounds typically stand about 63 to 74 cm at the shoulder and weigh roughly 23 to 27 kg.

faq.q: How long do Afghan Hounds live?
faq.a: A typical lifespan of about 12 to 14 years is often given, although one UK study found an average life expectancy of 11.1 years.

faq.q: Are Afghan Hounds easy to train?
faq.a: They have a reputation among trainers for slow obedience, and Stanley Coren's survey placed them last among the breeds ranked for obeying commands.

faq.q: Do Afghan Hounds need a lot of grooming?
faq.a: Yes. Their long, fine coat requires considerable care and grooming to stay in good condition.
